subject: Numeracy
title: Heavy and light
objectives: Children will compare two objects by weight.
Children will use a balance to check.
content: Heavy and light, heavier and lighter, and using a balance.
teachingActivities: Let children lift real objects and feel the difference before using a balance; teach that size does not always tell weight (a big balloon is light); use a simple pan or seesaw balance; say "the heavier side goes down".
learnerActivities: Compare two objects by weight and use a balance to check.
resources: Bags of sand and cotton wool
Pictures of heavy and light animals
assessment: Observe whether each child says which of two objects is heavier and uses a balance with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says which of two is heavier.

lessons.title: Heavy and light
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say heavy and light for different objects.
successCriteria: Lifts objects to feel the weight
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare size and length, count to 15, join and take away to 5 and make patterns.
resources: A bag of sand and a bag of cotton wool
Pictures of an elephant and a feather
lessons.starter: Hold a stone in one hand and a sponge in the other and say "The stone feels heavy. The sponge feels light."
teacherActivities: Let children hold two objects and say which feels heavy.
Say "Heavy things are hard to lift. Light things are easy."
Show pictures of an elephant and a feather.
Sort objects into heavy and light baskets.
learnerActivities: Children lift and say heavy or light.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Let children hold two objects and say which feels heavy. Children: Children lift and say heavy or light.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Heavy things are hard to lift. Light things are easy." Children: Children repeat heavy and light.
Step 3. Teacher: Show pictures of an elephant and a feather. Children: Child says heavy or light.
Step 4. Teacher: Sort objects into heavy and light baskets. Children: Child sorts the objects.

practical.title: Heavy and light baskets
steps: Put it in the heavy or light basket.
practical.safety: Use objects that children can lift easily and nothing with sharp edges. Supervise lifting and keep feet clear.

differentiation.support: Compare two objects that are very different in weight.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three objects that are heavier than a book.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the stone heavy or light?
Is the feather heavy or light?

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say heavy and light.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about heavy and light things at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say heavy and light for different objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Heavier and lighter
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will compare two objects and say which is heavier or lighter.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare size and length, count to 15, join and take away to 5 and make patterns.
resources: Pairs of objects of similar size
lessons.starter: Hold two bags of sand and say "Which one is heavier? Let us lift them and feel."
teacherActivities: Show two objects and let children lift one in each hand.
Compare size and weight: a big balloon and a small stone.
learnerActivities: Child points to the heavier one.
Child points to the lighter one.
Child says the balloon is light.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two objects and let children lift one in each hand. Children: Children lift and compare.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which is heavier?" Children: Child points to the heavier one.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which is lighter?" Children: Child points to the lighter one.
Step 4. Teacher: Compare size and weight: a big balloon and a small stone. Children: Child says the balloon is light.

practical.title: Lift and compare
practical.safety: Use objects that are safe to lift and keep them away from toes. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Compare objects with a very clear difference.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess before lifting.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say heavier and lighter.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two bags or fruits and say which is heavier.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "compare two objects and say which is heavier or lighter" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Using a balance
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use a balance to check which object is heavier.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare size and length, count to 15, join and take away to 5 and make patterns.
resources: Small objects such as blocks, stones and sponges
lessons.starter: Show a balance and say "The heavier side goes down. The lighter side goes up."
teacherActivities: Put a stone on one side and a sponge on the other.
Say "The stone side goes down. The stone is heavier."
Let each pair test two objects.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put a stone on one side and a sponge on the other. Children: Children watch the balance move.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "The stone side goes down. The stone is heavier." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each pair test two objects. Children: Pairs place objects and watch.
Step 4. Teacher: Say which is heavier. Children: Child says heavier or lighter.

practical.title: Balance test
practical.safety: Use a stable balance on a low table and light objects only. Supervise closely and keep fingers clear of the moving arm.

differentiation.support: Place the objects together and watch the balance.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two objects that balance.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the balance away and say heavier.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a simple balance with a hanger and bags at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use a balance to check which object is heavier" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Heavy or light hunt
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find heavy and light things and record them.
successCriteria: Finds a heavy and a light object
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare size and length, count to 15, join and take away to 5 and make patterns.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us find heavy things and light things around the room."
teacherActivities: Show how to lift a safe object and say heavy or light.
Put each object in the correct basket.
Check the baskets by comparing a heavy and a light object.
learnerActivities: Child finds an object and lifts it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to lift a safe object and say heavy or light. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children search for objects. Children: Child finds an object and lifts it.
Step 3. Teacher: Put each object in the correct basket. Children: Child sorts the object.
Step 4. Teacher: Check the baskets by comparing a heavy and a light object. Children: Child compares two objects.

practical.title: Weight hunt
steps: Put it in the heavy or light basket.
practical.safety: Only lift objects that are safe and small and never heavy furniture. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hunt in a small area with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to order three objects from lightest to heaviest.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What did you find that is heavy?
What did you find that is light?

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects back and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Find heavy and light things at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find heavy and light things and record them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 weight check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child compares weights.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare size and length, count to 15, join and take away to 5 and make patterns.
lessons.starter: Sing the heavy and light song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: lifting, balance and hunt.
At each station ask "Which is heavier?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: lifting, balance and hunt. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Which is heavier?" Children: Child lifts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Weight stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the balance on a low table. Use light objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and compare two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to order four objects by weight.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says heavy and light; says heavier and lighter; uses a balance; sorts by weight.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child compares weights" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
